'''Patrick J. Stover''' (born 1964) is an American nutrition scientist who researches [[B vitamin]]s. Currently a professor at [[Florida State University]], he is a fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] and a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]]. He has been co-[[editor-in-chief|editor]] of the ''[[Annual Review of Nutrition]]'' since 2015. He serves as a Deputy Editor of ''PNAS Nexus''.<ref>PNAS Nexus, Editorial Board, Oxford Academic. https://academic.oup.com/pnasnexus/pages/editorial-board?login=true</ref> He is the Co-Founder of the Institute of Connecting Nutrition and Health (ICON-Health) at Florida State University.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ICON Health |url=https://icon.fsu.edu/icon-health |access-date=2026-05-15 |website=ICON-Health |language=en}}</ref> 

==Early life and education==
Patrick J. Stover was born in 1964 to parents Katherine Hanlon and William Stover. His father, William H. Stover, was a decorated WWII veteran. As a Private First Class in the [[1st Marine Division]], he was awarded the [[Silver Star]] from the president of the United States “for conspicuous gallantry and intrepidity during action against enemy [[Guadalcanal campaign|Japanese forces on Guadalcanal]], Solomon Islands on November 3, 1942".<ref>{{Cite web|title=William Stover - Recipient -|url=http://valor.militarytimes.com/hero/38933|access-date=2021-01-22|website=valor.militarytimes.com|language=en}}</ref>

Stover grew up in rural Pennsylvania and he and his siblings were first generation college students.<ref>{{cite web|date=7 July 2001|title=William H. J. Stover|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/67403137/william-h-j-stover/|access-date=11 January 2021|work=The Philadelphia Inquirer|page=10}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://aglifesciences.tamu.edu/patrick-j-stover-biography/| title=Patrick J. Stover, PhD| website= Texas A&M College of Agriculture & Life Sciences| access-date=11 January 2021}}</ref> He attended [[Saint Joseph's University]] in Pennsylvania, graduating with a bachelor's degree in chemistry in 1986. He then graduated from [[VCU Medical Center]] in 1990 with a PhD in biochemistry and molecular biophysics.<ref name="NAS" /><ref>{{cite web|url=https://ecommons.cornell.edu/bitstream/handle/1813/40061/HENutrSci_PatrickStover.pdf;jsessionid=116CABBD1734B57BF6D25802BEA2B7EB?sequence=1| title=Patrick Stover| website=Cornell University| access-date=11 January 2021|year=2015}}</ref>

==Career==
Much of Stover's research centers on the [[B vitamin]]s [[folate]], [[vitamin B12|vitamin B<sub>12</sub>]] and [[riboflavin]].<ref name="NAS"/> Following the completion of his PhD, Stover had two [[postdoctoral]] appointments. The first was at VCU Medical Center from 1990 to 1991 with his PhD advisor Verne Schirch. Next, he went to the [[University of California, Berkeley]] to work with Barry Shane from 1992 to 1994. He served as Director of the Division of Nutritional Sciences at Cornell University from 2005 to 2018, a tenure of more than ten years.<ref>The Chicago Council on Global Affairs, "Patrick Stover." https://globalaffairs.org/research/experts/patrick-stover</ref><ref>National Academy of Sciences, "Patrick J. Stover." https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/patrick-j-stover-lpx1ac/</ref> In 2018, he was appointed Vice Chancellor and Dean for Agriculture and Life Sciences at Texas A&M University and Director of Texas A&M AgriLife Research.<ref>Texas A&M AgriLife Today, "Texas A&M hires new leader of agriculture college, agencies," Feb 8, 2018. https://agrilifetoday.tamu.edu/2018/02/08/texas-am-hires-new-leader-of-agriculture-college-agencies/</ref> As Vice Chancellor he oversaw more than 5,000 employees across the Texas A&M System’s four statewide agricultural agencies—AgriLife Research, the Texas A&M AgriLife Extension Service, the Texas A&M Forest Service, and the Texas A&M Veterinary Medical Diagnostic Laboratory—and as Dean led more than 7,800 students and 400 faculty members in 15 academic departments.<ref>Texas A&M AgriLife Today, "Stover designated as a Texas A&M University Distinguished Professor," Mar 3, 2020. https://agrilifetoday.tamu.edu/2020/03/03/stover-designated-as-a-texas-am-university-distinguished-professor/</ref> The Vice Chancellor and Dean administers agency funds of approximately $468 million per year, with the College of Agriculture and Life Sciences operating on an annual budget of approximately $53 million.<ref>Texas A&M AgriLife, Vice Chancellor & Dean position announcement (PDF). https://agrilife.org/wp-content/uploads/TAMU-VC-and-Dean-of-AgriLife-PD_Final.pdf</ref> During his tenure he directed new investment into academic departments, including more than $850,000 in financial commitments to recruit faculty and upgrade facilities in the Department of Poultry Science.<ref>Texas A&M AgriLife Today, "Texas A&M, poultry industry usher in new era in department," Jan 27, 2021. https://agrilifetoday.tamu.edu/2021/01/27/poultry-science/</ref> Stover established the Texas A&M Institute for Advancing Health through Agriculture (IHA) and served as its founding director.<ref>Florida State University, ICON-Health, "Patrick Stover." https://icon.fsu.edu/members/patrick-stover</ref><ref>National Academy of Sciences, "Patrick J. Stover." https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/patrick-j-stover-lpx1ac/</ref> He also established the Agriculture, Food, & Nutrition Evidence Center, located in Fort Worth, Texas.<ref>Texas A&M AgriLife Today, "Stover testifies in front of full House Committee on Agriculture," Jun 13, 2023. https://agrilifetoday.tamu.edu/2023/06/13/stover-testifies-in-front-of-full-house-committee-on-agriculture/</ref><ref>Texas A&M AgriLife, Agriculture, Food, and Nutrition Evidence Center, People (Fort Worth location). https://evidencecenter.tamu.edu/people/</ref> He stepped down as Vice Chancellor and Dean at the end of 2021 to focus full-time on standing up the Institute and the Evidence Center.<ref>Texas A&M Today, "Mark Hussey Named Acting Vice Chancellor and Dean of Agriculture and Life Sciences," Dec 15, 2021. https://stories.tamu.edu/news/2021/12/15/mark-hussey-named-acting-vice-chancellor-and-dean-of-agriculture-and-life-sciences/</ref> He has been co-[[editor-in-chief|editor]] of the ''[[Annual Review of Nutrition]]'' since 2015.<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1146/annurev-nu-35-071715-100001|title=Introduction|year=2015|last1=Stover|first1=Patrick J.|last2=Bowman|first2=Barbara|journal=Annual Review of Nutrition|volume=35 |article-number=annurev-nu-35-071715-100001 }}</ref>

He has made several fundamental discoveries by identifying new pathways in the field of folate biochemistry. These discoveries include identification of the pathway for the synthesis of 5-formyltetrahydrfolate, otherwise known as [[Folinic acid|lucovorin]],<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Stover|first1=P.|last2=Schirch|first2=V.|date=1990-08-25|title=Serine hydroxymethyltransferase catalyzes the hydrolysis of 5,10-methenyltetrahydrofolate to 5-formyltetrahydrofolate|journal=The Journal of Biological Chemistry|volume=265|issue=24|pages=14227–14233|doi=10.1016/S0021-9258(18)77290-6|issn=0021-9258|pmid=2201683|doi-access=free}}</ref> the regulation of folate metabolism by iron,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Fox|first1=Jennifer T.|last2=Stover|first2=Patrick J.|date=2009-11-06|title=Mechanism of the internal ribosome entry site-mediated translation of serine hydroxymethyltransferase 1|journal=The Journal of Biological Chemistry|volume=284|issue=45|pages=31085–31096|doi=10.1074/jbc.M109.035576|issn=1083-351X|pmc=2781508|pmid=19734143|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Woeller|first1=Collynn F.|last2=Fox|first2=Jennifer T.|last3=Perry|first3=Cheryll|last4=Stover|first4=Patrick J.|date=2007-10-12|title=A ferritin-responsive internal ribosome entry site regulates folate metabolism|journal=The Journal of Biological Chemistry|volume=282|issue=41|pages=29927–29935|doi=10.1074/jbc.M706264200|issn=0021-9258|pmid=17702748|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Oppenheim|first1=E. W.|last2=Adelman|first2=C.|last3=Liu|first3=X.|last4=Stover|first4=P. J.|date=2001-06-08|title=Heavy chain ferritin enhances serine hydroxymethyltransferase expression and de novo thymidine biosynthesis|journal=The Journal of Biological F.|last3=Chiang|first3=En-Pei|last4=Shane|first4=Barry|last5=Stover|first5=Patrick J.|date=2012-03-02|title=Serine hydroxymethyltransferase anchors de novo thymidylate synthesis pathway to nuclear lamina for DNA synthesis|journal=The Journal of Biological Chemistry|volume=287|issue=10|pages=7051–7062|doi=10.1074/jbc.M111.333120|issn=1083-351X|pmc=3293584|pmid=22235121|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=MacFarlane|first1=Amanda Stover has provided congressional testimony on nutrition and agriculture policy. In November 2021 he testified before the U.S. Senate Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry at its hearing “The State of Nutrition in America 2021.<ref>U.S. Senate Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition & Forestry, "The State of Nutrition in America 2021," Nov 2, 2021. https://www.agriculture.senate.gov/hearings/the-state-of-nutrition-in-america-2021</ref> In June 2023 he testified before the full U.S. House of Representatives Committee on Agriculture regarding diet-related chronic disease and federal nutrition programs.<ref>Texas A&M AgriLife Today, "Stover testifies in front of full House Committee on Agriculture," Jun 13, 2023. https://agrilifetoday.tamu.edu/2023/06/13/stover-testifies-in-front-of-full-house-committee-on-agriculture/</ref><ref>Environmental and Energy Study Institute, "Congressional Hearings Leading up to the 2023 Farm Bill: Part 5," Sep 14, 2023. https://www.eesi.org/articles/view/congressional-hearings-leading-up-to-the-2023-farm-bill-part-5</ref>

==Awards and honors==
He received a [[Presidential Early Career Award for Scientists and Engineers]] from President [[Bill Clinton]] in 1996. The [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] elected him as a fellow in 2014.<ref name="NAS"/> He served as president of the [[American Society for Nutrition]] from 2015 to 2016.<ref name="CV">{{cite web|url=https://agrilife.org/wp-content/uploads/Stover.CV_web.pdf| year=2017| title=Patrick J. Stover, PhD| website=Texas A&M Agrilife| access-date=11 January 2021}}</ref> In 2016 he was elected as a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="NAS">{{cite web|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/patrick-j-stover-lpx1ac/| title=Patrick Stover| website=National Academy of Sciences| access-date=11 January 2021}}</ref> In 2020 he was named a Texas A&M University Distinguished Professor, the university’s highest faculty honor.<ref>Texas A&M AgriLife Today, "Stover designated as a Texas A&M University Distinguished Professor," Mar 3, 2020. https://agrilifetoday.tamu.edu/2020/03/03/stover-designated-as-a-texas-am-university-distinguished-professor/</ref> In 2023 he was selected as the W.O. Atwater Memorial Lecturer by the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Agricultural Research Service.<ref>USDA Agricultural Research Service, "Enhancing the Purpose of Food" (2023 W.O. Atwater Memorial Lecture). https://www.ars.usda.gov/oc/utm/enhancing-the-purpose-of-food/</ref>

==Personal life==
He has four children.<ref name="hires">{{cite web|url=https://www.tamus.edu/texas-am-hires-new-leader-of-agriculture-college-agencies/| title=TEXAS A&M HIRES NEW LEADER OF AGRICULTURE COLLEGE, AGENCIES| date=8 February 2018| access-date=11 January 2021| website=Texas A&M University}}</ref>
